title: SQL vs NoSQL Databases Explained
intro: Both store data, but in very different ways. The right choice depends on your data and how you read it.

slides.heading: SQL databases
slides.subtitle: Tables with a fixed schema.
points: Rows and columns, like a spreadsheet

slides.heading: NoSQL databases
slides.subtitle: Flexible data models.
points: Often built to scale across many servers

slides.heading: Pick SQL when
slides.subtitle: Structure and correctness matter.
points: You need complex queries and reports

slides.heading: Pick NoSQL when
slides.subtitle: Flexibility and scale matter.
points: You mostly read data by a single key
You need very high write volume

scenario.situation: A team builds a banking app on a document database because it felt quicker to start.
scenario.problem: A transfer updates two accounts, and keeping both balances consistent becomes complicated and error-prone.
scenario.fix: Use a relational database with transactions. Both updates succeed together or fail together.
scenario.takeaway: Choose by your data and its rules, not by hype.

cta: SQL or NoSQL for your current project?
